title: Cross-user secret use
impact: A normal Member can make Runloop use another user's private API key or secret when the gateway ID is known.
proof: The Member could not list or open the private gateway. The Member supplied its ID during an agent launch. Runloop then used the gateway owner's test credential.
limit: A known gateway ID and same-organization access were confirmed. Cross-organization use was not proven.
fix: Check the owner and organization each time Runloop uses a gateway ID.

title: Tenant Owner controls global flags
impact: A self-service tenant Owner can reach a platform-level write path for feature flags that apply across the whole Runloop deployment.
proof: The account was denied platform-admin routes. SPYDR listed global flags and replayed the current value of one global flag. Runloop returned HTTP 200 and the value stayed unchanged.
limit: No live global value was changed. Further admin privilege escalation was not tested.
fix: Require platform-admin permission for every read or write of a global flag.

title: SSRF from the sandbox
impact: A sandbox user can make a Runloop gateway send requests to services on the local network outside the sandbox.
proof: A test callback showed that the request came from a Runloop gateway service, not the Devbox. A local network target returned a live HTTP response.
limit: No cloud credential, metadata token, or internal secret was obtained.
fix: Block private network addresses before each request and after each redirect.

title: OAuth SSRF before agent launch
impact: A user can make Reflex send an OAuth registration request to a service on the local network before any agent runs.
proof: Before an MCP setup or agent existed, the Reflex server fetched a selected OAuth file. A test redirect sent its registration request to a local address.
limit: No cloud token or internal response body was obtained through this path.
fix: Allow only public HTTPS addresses during OAuth setup. Check the address again after each redirect.

title: SSRF with response data
impact: A user can make Runloop fetch a selected address and return part of the response. Reachable service data can appear in the error.
proof: A test server returned a unique marker in an HTTP 500 response. The same marker appeared in the MCP connection error shown to the user.
limit: The response oracle was proven with an owned marker. Sensitive internal data was not accessed.
fix: Allow only public HTTPS addresses. Check each redirect. Do not show server response bodies to the user.

title: CLI arbitrary file read
impact: An agent connected to a Mac can read files outside the selected folder with the permissions of the connected Mac user.
proof: The file tool blocked a test file outside the selected folder. The command tool read the same file from the connected Mac.
limit: The read used the connected Mac user's permissions. No privilege escalation was shown.
fix: Apply the selected folder limit to commands and subprocesses, not only the file tool.
